recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-6032 unless the work group reopens the broader DocumentReference minimum-cardinality policy.
issue_request: FHIR-6032 was a Published/Persuasive SD change request from DSTU1 saying DocumentReference was too XDS-oriented and had too many required elements when used merely to reference a document. The final resolution narrowed the applied change to moving DocumentReference.author to 0..*.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 70f650c74d8b6b08adb3a34f9e21acbcd6fddcc3 (#6032, svn revision 6185), which changed the then-authoritative DocumentReference spreadsheet cardinality for DocumentReference.author from 1..* to 0..*. That historical spreadsheet source is no longer present in the current checkout after later source refactoring.
additional_context: DocumentReference is an active resource in source/fhir.ini. The current authoritative source is source/documentreference/structuredefinition-DocumentReference.xml, where DocumentReference.author remains 0..*, DocumentReference.type and the former indexed field now represented as DocumentReference.date are optional, and DocumentReference.status remains the only required element among the Jira-described set. Later DocumentReference refactors retained the optional author cardinality. Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-6032 and DocumentReference.author found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the active current source already preserves the applied Jira decision and the broader cardinality state described by the issue. Adding new prose or changing cardinalities would be redundant and could exceed the published resolution.
